issues.message: getUserOrderDetails nests callbacks five levels deep (fetchUser -> fetchOrders -> forEach -> fetchShipping), exceeding the nesting-depth limit of 4 and creating classic callback hell.
issues.suggestedFix: Promisify fetchUser/fetchOrders/fetchShipping and rewrite with async/await plus Promise.all over orders to flatten the control flow.

issues.message: loadDashboard chains nested .then() calls with no error handling and wraps them in an unnecessary Promise constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Convert to a single async function using await for each fetch and add a try/catch (or .catch) for error handling; drop the explicit Promise wrapper.

issues.message: The async control flow uses else branches for error handling instead of guard-clause early returns, increasing nesting and cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Use early-return guard clauses (if (err) return cb(err)) to eliminate the else branches once converted to async/await.

complexity-review.summary: Severe callback hell and unstructured, error-handling-free promise chains make this async code unmaintainable; confidence High.

issues.message: aggregateByRegion nests for/if blocks five levels deep, exceeding the nesting-depth limit of 4.

issues.message: findDuplicateEntries nests four for loops plus an inner if (five levels), exceeding the nesting-depth limit of 4.
issues.suggestedFix: Extract the inner comparison loop into a named helper, or build an index/map of value-to-positions to detect duplicates without quadruple nesting.

issues.message: processNestedConfig nests loops and type-check ifs five levels deep, exceeding the nesting-depth limit of 4.
issues.suggestedFix: Extract the array-scanning block into a checkSectionKey helper and use guard clauses to reduce indentation.

complexity-review.summary: All three functions exceed the nesting-depth limit of 4 (each reaching five levels), making the control flow hard to follow; confidence High.

issues.message: processTransaction is roughly 70 lines, well over the 20-line function-size limit.

issues.message: processTransaction declares 7 parameters, exceeding the parameter limit of 5.

issues.message: processTransaction contains well over 10 branches (validation, discount if/else chain, payment-method if/else chain, dry-run, retry), exceeding the cyclomatic-complexity limit of 10.

issues.message: Discount and payment-method handling use long if/else-if chains rather than guard clauses or table lookups, raising cognitive load.

issues.message: push() mutates the module-level taskQueue array.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a new array: taskQueue = [...taskQueue, task] or have callers build new state.

issues.message: push() inside forEach mutates the module-level taskQueue array.
issues.suggestedFix: Build a new array with [...taskQueue, ...tasks] instead of pushing in a loop.

issues.message: sort() mutates the tasks parameter in place.
issues.suggestedFix: Use [...tasks].sort(...) or tasks.toSorted(...).

issues.message: splice() mutates the tasks parameter in place.
issues.suggestedFix: Use slice + spread: [...tasks.slice(0, index), ...tasks.slice(index + 1)].

issues.message: splice() insert mutates the tasks parameter in place.
issues.suggestedFix: Use [...tasks.slice(0, index), task, ...tasks.slice(index)].

issues.message: reverse() mutates the tasks parameter in place.
issues.suggestedFix: Use [...tasks].reverse() or tasks.toReversed().

issues.message: splice() mutates the tasks parameter while iterating it.
issues.suggestedFix: Use filter to partition: tasks.filter(t => !t.completed) for the remainder and tasks.filter(t => t.completed) for the result.

issues.message: sort() mutates the tasks parameter in place.
issues.suggestedFix: Use [...tasks].sort(...) or tasks.toSorted(...).

js-fp-review.summary: Pervasive array mutation: push on a module-level array (external state) plus in-place sort/splice/reverse on parameters throughout.

issues.message: appVersion is declared let but never reassigned.
issues.suggestedFix: Change to const appVersion = "1.0.0".

issues.message: ++ used on requestCount outside a loop counter.
issues.suggestedFix: Avoid the increment; compute a new value or return requestCount + 1 from a pure function.

issues.message: Mutates external state via window.localStorage.
issues.suggestedFix: Isolate the side effect at the boundary and pass values in/out as data.

issues.message: Assigns a property on the global window object.
issues.suggestedFix: Store feature flags in a passed-in state object instead of window.

issues.message: Mutates process.env.NODE_ENV.
issues.suggestedFix: Read config from injected values; do not write to process.env at runtime.

issues.message: Mutates process.env.APP_VERSION.
issues.suggestedFix: Pass version through configuration rather than writing process.env.

issues.message: Mutates window.location.href (global state).
issues.suggestedFix: Return the target URL and let a thin boundary perform navigation.

issues.message: ++ used on requestCount outside a loop counter.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a new count value instead of incrementing shared state.

issues.message: debugMode is declared let but reassigned only via the impure enableDebug; consider const + functional state.
issues.suggestedFix: Model debug state as passed-in/returned data rather than a mutable module-level let.

issues.message: Reassigns module-level debugMode (external state mutation).
issues.suggestedFix: Return new state instead of mutating the shared debugMode variable.

issues.message: Mutates process.env.DEBUG.
issues.suggestedFix: Pass debug config in rather than writing process.env at runtime.

issues.message: Assigns a handler onto the global window object.
issues.suggestedFix: Register handlers through a passed-in registry instead of window.

issues.message: label is declared let but never reassigned.
issues.suggestedFix: Change to const label.

js-fp-review.summary: Heavy global-state mutation (window.*, process.env.*, module-level reassignment) compounded by let-that-should-be-const and ++ outside loops.
Immutable throughout: const everywhere, Object.freeze, and spread-based updates that return new state without mutation.

issues.message: Mutates the profile parameter's name property.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a new object: { ...profile, name: profile.name.trim() }.

issues.message: Mutates the profile parameter's email property.
issues.suggestedFix: Include email in the returned spread copy instead of assigning.

issues.message: Object.assign writes into the existing profile.metadata object.
issues.suggestedFix: Use { ...profile, metadata: { ...profile.metadata, ...extra } }.

issues.message: Object.assign mutates the profile parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Build a new object: { ...profile, role: profile.role ?? "viewer", metadata: profile.metadata ?? {} }.

issues.message: delete mutates the profile parameter by removing legacyField.
issues.suggestedFix: Destructure it out: const { legacyField, ...rest } = profile; return rest.

issues.message: Assigns into the nested profile.metadata object (parameter mutation).
issues.suggestedFix: Return { ...profile, metadata: { ...profile.metadata, [key]: value } }.

issues.message: Mutates the profile parameter's role property.
issues.suggestedFix: Return { ...profile, role: "admin" }.

js-fp-review.summary: Every function mutates its profile parameter via property assignment, Object.assign on existing objects, or delete rather than returning new objects.
Pure transforms using map/filter/reduce/slice with spread copies; no mutation of parameters or external state.
All sorting/reversing uses non-mutating toSorted/toReversed or spread-copy-then-sort, leaving inputs untouched.

naming-review.summary: Variables reveal intent, functions describe actions, booleans use is/has prefixes, and collections are pluralized with no magic values.

issues.message: User-controlled sort parameter is concatenated into the ORDER BY clause, allowing SQL injection.

issues.message: User-controlled name is interpolated into a LIKE clause via template literal.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a parameterized query with $1 and pass the wildcard pattern as a bound value.

issues.message: Login query concatenates username and password into SQL, enabling authentication bypass.
issues.suggestedFix: Parameterize the query and verify the password via a hash comparison, never via SQL string matching.

issues.message: User-controlled id is concatenated into a DELETE statement.

security-review.summary: Four SQL injection sinks via string concatenation, including a classic auth-bypass login query. Confidence: High. ci_dirs_scanned: []

issues.message: User-controlled query param is reflected unescaped into the HTML response.

issues.message: Unsanitized user comment is injected into an inline script and assigned to innerHTML, enabling stored/reflected XSS.

issues.message: User-controlled username is injected into an inline script and passed to document.write, enabling DOM XSS.

issues.message: Error handler reflects err.message and the request path unescaped into the response, exposing internals and adding another XSS sink.

svelte-review.summary: Correct onMount/onDestroy pairing and $effect cleanup returns for all listeners, timers, and observers; no reactivity issues.

issues.message: createTodoManager backs its state with a plain closure array `todos` that Svelte cannot reactively observe, so UI consumers never update.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare the state with $state (e.g., `let todos = $state<string[]>([])`) in a .svelte.ts rune module so mutations are tracked.

issues.message: The `items` getter returns the internal `todos` array reference directly, exposing mutable closure state with no reactive tracking.
issues.suggestedFix: Back `todos` with $state and return a defensive copy (`return [...todos]`).

issues.message: getAll() returns the internal array reference, letting callers mutate it without triggering any reactive update.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a copy: `return [...todos]` (or structuredClone for nested data).

issues.message: createCounter holds mutable `value` in a closure outside $state, so the `current` getter is not reactively tracked.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `let value = $state(0)` so increments trigger reactivity.

svelte-review.summary: Factory functions back component state with plain closures and expose internal references, producing silent reactivity breakage.

issues.message: $effect reads and writes `count` in the same effect, risking an infinite reactive loop.
issues.suggestedFix: Move the reset out of the effect or guard it so the effect does not write a value it depends on; consider an event handler instead.

issues.message: $effect is used to compute synchronous derived state `doubled = count * 2`, which should be a $derived.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with `const doubled = $derived(count * 2)` and remove the $state declaration.

issues.message: $derived contains side effects (console.log and fetch), which belong in $effect, not $derived.
issues.suggestedFix: Make `summary` a pure `$derived(`Count is ${count}`)` and move the fetch/log into a separate $effect.

issues.message: $effect computes derived value `label` from `count`, which should use $derived.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace with `const label = $derived(count > 5 ? 'high' : 'low')`.

issues.message: $effect both reads and writes `items` (assigns a default when filtered count is zero), risking an infinite loop.
issues.suggestedFix: Compute `filteredCount` with $derived and handle the default-item logic outside the reactive read path.

svelte-review.summary: Multiple $effect misuses: writing to own dependencies, using $effect for derived state, and side effects inside $derived.

issues.message: querySelector runs at module/component-init scope before onMount, accessing the DOM before the component is mounted.
issues.suggestedFix: Move the DOM read into onMount or an $effect so it runs after mount.

issues.message: The scroll event listener added in onMount is never removed, leaking the listener after unmount.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a cleanup from onMount (or use $effect) that calls window.removeEventListener for the scroll handler.

issues.message: setInterval is started in onMount with no clearInterval, so the timer keeps running after the component unmounts.
issues.suggestedFix: Capture the interval id and clearInterval it in an onMount cleanup return or onDestroy.

issues.message: The $effect reads `items` but calls processItems which reads `config.multiplier`, a hidden dependency the effect never tracks, so it won't re-run when config changes.
issues.suggestedFix: Read `config.multiplier` directly in the effect/derived body, or use `const processed = $derived(items.map(n => n * config.multiplier))`.

issues.message: The ResizeObserver created in onMount is never disconnected, leaking the observer after unmount.
issues.suggestedFix: Return a cleanup from onMount (or use $effect) that calls observer.disconnect().

svelte-review.summary: DOM accessed before mount, multiple listeners/timers/observers leak without cleanup, and an $effect has a hidden config dependency.
Correct use of $state, $derived for computed values, $effect with cleanup for side effects, and defensive copies on full reassignment; no reactivity issues.
All manual store subscriptions are cleaned up in onDestroy and one-time reads use get(); no subscription leaks.

issues.message: Destructuring a $state object into `text` and `done` captures plain values that no longer participate in proxy tracking.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the state object intact and access `state.text`/`state.done`, or derive each value with $derived rather than destructuring.

issues.message: toggleFirst mutates a nested array (`todos[0].tags.push`) without reassignment, which may not trigger fine-grained reactivity.
issues.suggestedFix: Reassign through the proxy, e.g., `todos[0].tags = [...todos[0].tags, 'updated']` (or mutate via the tracked proxy path).

issues.message: markDone mutates a deep property without reassigning the parent, which may not propagate a UI update.
issues.suggestedFix: Reassign the item, e.g., `todos[index] = { ...todos[index], done: true }`.

issues.message: Spreading a $state object into a plain object (`{...todos[0]}`) produces a non-reactive snapshot.
issues.suggestedFix: Use `$state.snapshot(todos[0])` if a plain serializable copy is intended, and avoid treating the result as reactive.

issues.message: Assigning a pre-existing plain object from the API into `todos[0]` expects deep tracking, but nested props of the plain object may not be reactively proxied as expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Assign through $state so the value is wrapped, e.g., reassign the whole `todos` array with the new data so Svelte proxies it.

svelte-review.summary: Multiple $state proxy pitfalls: destructuring, deep mutation without reassignment, spreading into plain objects, and assigning plain objects expecting deep tracking.

issues.message: userStore.subscribe() is called with no corresponding unsubscribe in onDestroy, leaking the subscription on unmount.
issues.suggestedFix: Capture the returned unsubscribe and call it in onDestroy, or use the `$userStore` auto-subscription syntax.

issues.message: themeStore.subscribe() returns `unsub` but it is never invoked in onDestroy, leaking the subscription.
issues.suggestedFix: Call `unsub()` inside an onDestroy callback.

issues.message: The derived store displayName.subscribe() has no cleanup, leaking the subscription.
issues.suggestedFix: Store the returned unsubscribe and call it in onDestroy, or use `$displayName` auto-subscription.

issues.message: A subscription created inside onMount returns no cleanup and is not handled in onDestroy, leaking on unmount.
issues.suggestedFix: Return the unsubscribe from onMount or register it in onDestroy.

svelte-review.summary: Multiple manual store subscriptions are created with no unsubscribe in onDestroy, causing memory leaks on unmount.

issues.message: A single module-level CartService instance is shared and mutated across tests with no beforeEach reset, making tests order-dependent.

issues.message: Truthiness-only assertions (toBeTruthy on user, name, email) verify presence but not the actual returned values, so wrong data passes.

test-design-advisor.report:
## Test Design — currency formatter (cents → display string)

### Testability
| Unit | Testable as-is? | Blocker | Seam (testability-patterns.md) |
|------|-----------------|---------|--------------------------------|
| `formatCents(amount)` | Yes | None — pure function, no I/O / clock / RNG / global state | None needed |

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| cents → display string (`1050`→`"$10.50"`, `0`→`"$0.00"`, negatives→`"-$1.00"`) | unit | — | — (no stack declared; name profile when known) | Pure logic / branches / edge cases — heuristic #1: Unit, always. Lowest layer that meaningfully verifies it. |

(`Tool` = no profile: stack undeclared. Resolve from `test-stack-profiles/<stack>.md` once the manifest is known.)

### Gate analysis
No behavior pre-gate fires: not user-facing (Gate A), not a bug fix (Gate B), no HTMX/Alpine/Turbo swap (Gate C), no visual artifact (Gate D). Silent — pick stays at unit.

### Double strategy
| Test | Collaborator | Double | Verify by |
|------|--------------|--------|-----------|
| all cases | none | none | state (assert returned string) |

### Redundancy check
Not business-critical (not labelled); single-layer unit coverage is correct. No second layer needed.

### Next edit
Write a parameterized unit test (Four-Phase: Setup input → Exercise `formatCents` → Verify string) covering `1050`, `0`, a negative, and boundary cases.

## Test Design — "Add to cart" updates header cart badge (no full reload)

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| new item count is computed correctly | unit | — | — (no profile: stack undeclared) | Pure logic / edge cases — push to lowest layer. |
| `POST add-to-cart` persists and returns updated count | integration | — | — (e.g. MockMvc/supertest once stack known) | Real adapter/serialization/wiring (heuristic #2). |
| badge re-renders with new count after click (user acts and must *see* it) | E2E | → cd-test-architecture | — (real browser harness, deferred) | **Gate A** — user-facing dynamic: user acts and must see a rendered result through front end + API + header re-render. E2E **alongside** the lower layers. |

### Gate analysis
**Gate A — user-facing dynamic fires.** The user clicks and must *see* the correctly rendered badge in the browser; the flow spans front end → API → header re-render. → E2E **alongside** unit + integration. Cost: E2E is slow/flaky; amortize by folding the badge assertion into a broader add-to-cart **journey** test. Application-level E2E architecture is deferred — **→ cd-test-architecture**.

## Test Design — checkout discount bug (10% on $200 shows $10, should be $20)

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| 10% coupon on $200 = $20 discount (root math) | unit | — | — | The actual defect is a calculation — pin the math at unit level where it's fast and precise. |
| checkout page **displays** the correct discount | E2E | ↑E2E (Gate B regression) | → cd-test-architecture | **Gate B** — bug discovered **in the browser at checkout**; regression goes at the **discovery layer** = E2E/browser. Must fail on old code, pass on the fix. |

### Gate analysis
**Gate B — bug-fix regression fires.** The defect was discovered in the browser at the checkout page → regression at the **layer the bug was discovered** (browser → E2E). Gate B **never escalates above the discovery layer**. The regression test must fail on the old code and pass on the fix. Separately, the root-cause math should still be pinned at unit level. The browser regression's harness is deferred **→ cd-test-architecture**.

### Redundancy check
Discount-at-checkout is plausibly business-critical (revenue). Covered at two layers with different failure modes — unit (catches the math, misses rendering) and E2E (catches the rendered symptom, slow/flaky).

## Test Design — CSV row parser off-by-one (drops last row)

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| parser returns all N rows (3-row file → 3 rows) | unit | ↑unit (Gate B regression, at discovery layer) | — | Pure parsing logic / edge case — heuristic #1: Unit. Bug was found at unit level, so the regression also lives here. |

### Gate analysis
**Gate B — bug-fix regression fires.** The defect was **discovered while running the parser's unit tests** → regression at the discovery layer = **unit**. Gate B never escalates above the discovery layer, so no integration/E2E is warranted. The regression must fail on the old (off-by-one) code and pass on the fix.

### Redundancy check
Not labelled business-critical; single-layer unit coverage at the discovery layer is correct and sufficient. No second layer.

## Test Design — cart quantity change: HTMX POST + DB write + fragment swap into #order-total

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| new order total computed for a quantity | unit | — | — (candidate `ssr-htmx`) | Pure logic — lowest layer. |
| `POST /cart/item` persists new qty and returns correct HTML fragment | integration | — | — (candidate `ssr-htmx`) | Real persistence + serialization/wiring (heuristic #2); catches routing/persistence, **misses client swap**. |
| HTMX swaps the returned fragment into `#order-total` (`hx-target`/`hx-swap="outerHTML"`) | component / browser | browser **REQUIRED** (Gate C) | — (candidate `ssr-htmx`: browser test) | **Gate C** — HTMX dynamic-swap delivery chain. Integration is **complementary, not sufficient**; the structural seam only manifests in a real browser. |

### Gate analysis
**Gate C — dynamic-swap delivery chain fires.** An HTMX swap → **browser test REQUIRED** (not "recommended") for the seam. Holds even though there *is* a server state change: integration covers the mutation + fragment payload, but the swap into `#order-total` (target correctness, `outerHTML` replacement, any re-init) is a client-side structural seam a browser test alone proves. The two layers are complementary — keep both.

## Test Design — Alpine.js "Show details" toggle (x-show, no server call)

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| clicking "Show details" toggles panel visibility (`@click="open = !open"` → `x-show`) | component / browser | browser **REQUIRED** (Gate C) | — (candidate Alpine profile) | **Gate C** — Alpine dynamic-swap delivery chain. Holds **with no server state change** (Gate C explicitly covers the structural seam: directive wiring, `x-show` toggle, re-init). A real browser is required to verify the user-visible toggle. |

### Gate analysis
**Gate C — dynamic-swap delivery chain fires.** Alpine.js `@click`→`x-show` is a client-side dynamic swap → **browser test REQUIRED**. The fixture explicitly states **no server call**; Gate C holds with no server state change because the seam is structural. There is no logic to push lower — the boolean flip is not a meaningful unit. No integration layer (no network/persistence).

### Redundancy check
Not labelled business-critical (a details disclosure toggle); single-layer browser/component coverage is appropriate. No second layer.

## Test Design — invoice PDF generation

### Behavior pre-gates
**Gate D — visual fidelity FIRED.** Output is a PDF whose layout/appearance matters, and a signed-off **reference** mockup exists. Per `test-layer-gates.md`, with a reference: **approval (text)** for the textual content and/or **screenshot** for CSS/layout. Surface the maintenance cost of both. No app-level E2E is mandated, so this stays at unit/module altitude.

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| Totals/tax/line-item math | unit | — | no profile: <stack> | Pure logic, branches, edge cases — lowest layer that verifies it |
| Rendered invoice textual content vs reference | integration | ↑integration | no profile: <stack> | Exercises the real renderer to produce the artifact compared against the signed-off reference (approval) |
| Rendered invoice visual layout vs reference | integration | ↑integration | no profile: <stack> | Visual layout fidelity needs the rendered artifact compared to the design file (screenshot) |

### Technique overlay
| Behavior | Technique | Cost note |
|----------|-----------|-----------|
| Rendered textual content vs reference (approval.md) | approval | A signed-off reference exists; approved output must be re-approved on every intentional change |
| Rendered visual layout vs reference (screenshot.md) | screenshot | Pixel/region snapshots are brittle to font/render-engine drift |

### Next edit
Extract total/tax computation into a pure function and unit-test it; then add an approval test of the rendered text and a screenshot test of the layout, both anchored to the signed-off reference file.

## Test Design — transactional HTML email render

### Behavior pre-gates
**Gate D — visual fidelity FIRED.** An HTML email is an output whose layout/appearance matters. There is **no reference or mockup**, so per `test-layer-gates.md` the no-reference branch applies: **manual review + suggest creating a reference**. Correctness is currently visual judgment — recommend capturing a signed-off reference so an approval (text) and/or screenshot (layout) test can replace the manual gate.

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| Order data → template model (greeting, items, total, footer) | unit | — | no profile: <stack> | Pure logic — lowest layer that verifies content selection/formatting |
| Rendered HTML contains correct content tokens | integration | ↑integration | no profile: <stack> | Exercises the real template engine; asserts presence/correctness of key fields in output |
| Overall visual layout/appearance | manual | ↑manual | — | No reference exists; manual review until a reference is created (then escalate to approval/screenshot) |

### Next edit
Extract the order→template-model mapping into a pure function and unit-test it; then create a signed-off reference email so the currently-manual visual gate can become an approval/screenshot test.

## Test Design — funds-transfer amount calculation

### Behavior pre-gates
None of Gates A/B/C/D fire — no user-facing dynamic action, no bug-fix regression context, no dynamic-swap chain, no visual artifact.

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| Fee/overdraft/debit-credit math | unit | — | no profile: <stack> | Pure logic, edge cases — lowest layer (already covered) |
| Debit+credit persisted atomically across the transaction boundary | integration | — | no profile: <stack> | Routing/persistence/atomicity needs a real DB + transaction manager — a different failure mode than the calculation |

### Redundancy check (business-critical) — FIRED
This behavior is labelled **business-critical** (an error moves real money) and is covered at **only one layer** (a single unit test of the calculation). Per the catches/misses table in `test-layer-gates.md`, **unit catches** logic/edge cases but **misses** wiring, integration, and persistence. Recommend a **second** layer — **integration** — with a different **failure mode**: verify the debit and credit are persisted **atomically** (both commit or both roll back). The single unit test cannot catch a half-applied transfer where the math is right but the transaction boundary leaks.

### Next edit
Add an integration test (real test-container DB) that asserts debit+credit atomicity and overdraft rollback around the transaction boundary — covering the failure mode the lone unit test misses.

## Test Design — live coupon-discount total update (bug fix)

### Behavior pre-gates — TWO gates fire at once
**Gate B — bug-fix regression FIRED.** The bug was discovered **in the browser** (displayed total doesn't update). → regression at the **discovery layer = E2E**. Must fail on old code, pass on the fix. Never escalates above the discovery layer.

**Gate A — user-facing dynamic FIRED.** The user acts (applies a coupon) and must **see** the total re-render live. → E2E **alongside** lower layers. Slow/flaky cost applies; amortize by extending the existing coupon-apply journey test.

**Gate union.** Both gates land on **E2E** — union to a single layer (no duplicate). Both costs reconcile to the same advice: one browser-level test that is *both* the failing regression and the dynamic-update journey assertion. Because this mandates application-level E2E/browser architecture, flag the seam **`→ cd-test-architecture`** and defer the harness/pipeline design there.

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| Discounted-total math (coupon applied) | unit | — | no profile: <stack> | Pure logic — fast precise regression of the value |
| Coupon endpoint returns discounted total | integration | — | no profile: <stack> | Routing/serialization of the discounted total over the wire |
| Displayed total re-renders live on apply (no reload) | E2E | → cd-test-architecture | no profile: <stack> | User-facing dynamic + browser-discovered bug; the live DOM update is only verifiable in a real browser |

### Next edit
Write the browser-level regression that fails on current code (total stale until reload) and passes after the fix (total re-renders live on coupon apply), folded into the existing coupon journey; defer the harness design `→ cd-test-architecture`. Also pin the discounted-total math with a unit test.

## Test Design — "Apply filter" updates product listing

### Behavior pre-gates — AMBIGUOUS, asking once
Whether a browser-level dynamic gate applies is genuinely unclear: the description does not say if "Apply filter" is a **client-side dynamic** update (results re-render in place, no reload — would fire **Gate C** dynamic-swap, browser test REQUIRED, and **Gate A** user-facing dynamic → E2E) or a **full server-side round-trip** that reloads the page (no browser dynamic gate; integration over the filtered endpoint suffices).

Per the skill, dynamic-ness is ambiguous, so I **state the assumption and ask once** rather than escalate silently:

> **Question (batched):** Is "Apply filter" a client-side dynamic in-place update (HTMX/Alpine/Turbo/JS swap, no reload) or a full server round-trip that reloads the page? **Treat all as dynamic?** — if yes, I escalate to a REQUIRED browser test (Gate C) plus an E2E journey (Gate A).

**Default assumption pending your answer:** treated as a full server round-trip (no dynamic gate fires) — the conservative non-escalating read.

### Pyramid placement
| Behavior | Layer | Gate | Tool | Why this layer |
|----------|-------|------|------|----------------|
| Filter predicate / result matching | unit | — | no profile: <stack> | Pure logic — lowest layer that verifies which products match |
| Apply-filter request returns the filtered listing | integration | — | no profile: <stack> | Routing/serialization of the filtered result set over the endpoint |
| Results re-render in place on apply (no reload) | browser | (conditional: ↑browser **if** confirmed client-side dynamic — Gate C REQUIRED + Gate A E2E) | no profile: <stack> | Only verifiable in a real browser; included *only if* the dynamic-swap answer is yes |

### Next edit
Unit-test the filter predicate now; in parallel confirm whether "Apply filter" is a client-side dynamic swap or a server round-trip. If dynamic, add a REQUIRED browser test for the in-place swap (Gate C) and an E2E journey (Gate A); if a round-trip, the integration test on the filtered endpoint is sufficient.
